title: Day 955: Board of Peace Asks UN Security Council to Press Hamas to Disarm — Calls Hamas Demilitarization 'Non-Negotiable'; Gaza Ceasefire Described as 'Stalled'
detail: On May 19, 2026 (Day 955 / Ceasefire Day 222), the UN Security Council convened a high-level meeting on Gaza during which Trump's Board of Peace — chaired by former UN envoy Nickolay Mladenov — formally requested the Council to press Hamas to begin the disarmament process, describing it as 'not negotiable' and the central sticking point blocking progress on the October 2025 ceasefire's Phase Two. The Board of Peace presented its report to the Security Council, calling the Gaza ceasefire 'stalled' since October 10, 2025. Mladenov's framework had set four Phase Two deadlines (April 11, 14, 19, and a late-April window) that all passed without Hamas agreement. Hamas rejected the Board of Peace report as a 'dubious attempt to muddy the waters,' reiterating it would not discuss disarmament without a guaranteed Israeli withdrawal and a political horizon toward Palestinian statehood — conditions Netanyahu's coalition refused to accept. The UNSC meeting followed the Security Council's May 17 open debate in which the UN Deputy Special Coordinator documented 2,400+ Israeli ceasefire violations and 857+ Palestinian deaths since October 10, 2025. Israel controls approximately 60% of Gaza, far beyond the ceasefire's Yellow Line boundaries. The Board of Peace's escalation of pressure on Hamas at the UNSC level represents the most direct multilateral push to break the Phase Two deadlock. Phase Two would require Hamas to decommission offensive weapons over eight months while Israel progressively withdraws, in exchange for reconstruction funding (UN-EU-WB estimate: $71.4B needed). IDF operational plans for a resumed ground offensive are reported complete, pending US authorization. The accountability dimension of the Board of Peace meeting is significant: it occurred the same week that the killing of Hamas military chief Izz al-Din al-Haddad and the appointment of his successor Mohammed Odeh demonstrated Hamas's continued command reconstitution despite sustained Israeli targeting.

media.caption: UN Security Council holds high-level meeting on Gaza before Trump's Board of Peace convenes — PBS NewsHour, May 19, 2026

title: Day 955: Kallner October 7 Inquiry Bill Advances Toward First Knesset Plenum Reading — 42 Days to Supreme Court July 1 Accountability Deadline
detail: On May 19, 2026 (Day 955 / Ceasefire Day 222), with 42 days remaining until the Israeli Supreme Court's July 1, 2026 accountability deadline, the Knesset coalition's October 7 inquiry bill sponsored by Likud MK Ariel Kallner continued advancing toward a first plenum reading expected in late May 2026. The bill — revealed on May 13 to have quietly dropped language requiring 'a full, thorough, and independent investigation' from its purpose clause, and barring current or former Supreme Court justices from serving on the panel — had passed a preliminary Knesset reading amid fierce opposition from bereaved family organizations, the October Council, former hostages, and legal experts who called it a 'political whitewash.' The opposition Beyachad alliance of Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid, formed on May 11, pledged an independent state commission of inquiry as the first act of any alternative government. A JPPI poll published May 15 found 63% of Israelis support an immediate independent commission. The ongoing accountability crisis intersects directly with the Board of Peace's May 19 UNSC push: Israel's far-right coalition has indicated that renewed military operations in Gaza would help avoid an accountability reckoning, while Netanyahu's CBS 60 Minutes interview (analyzed on May 12) marked his first partial admission of shared responsibility for October 7 — 'everybody bears some responsibility, from the prime minister down' — without committing to a specific investigation mechanism. The High Court of Justice's two-month extension given on April 27, 2026 established July 1 as a hard deadline; what form of investigation — independent, parliamentary, or political — Israel presents to the court will determine whether the judicial standoff escalates further.

media.caption: Contentious law for politically appointed Oct. 7 probe passes preliminary Knesset reading — Times of Israel
